name: the Omo valley, in the East African Rift
labels: where the Omo I and II skulls were found
veg: Savanna, bushland and river forest, much as today, since the Kibish valley has no towns or fields (ESA WorldCover). Sources: Omo Kibish Formation studies (Brown & Fuller 2008; McDougall et al. 2005).

name: the Nile valley
veg: Desert cliffs above a green floodplain of grass, reeds and trees, in place of today's irrigated fields and villages. Source: Nile Basin state-of-basin report (environment chapter).

name: Galilee, in the Levant
veg: Last-glacial steppe with dwarf shrubs and few oaks. Sources: Miebach et al., Dead Sea pollen; EGU2015-3841 (southern Levant, last glacial).

name: Hatay, on the coast of Anatolia
veg: A mosaic of Mediterranean woodland and open steppe. Source: Kuhn et al. 2009, Üçağızlı Cave (J. Hum. Evol.).

name: the Iron Gates gorge of the Danube
labels: the Kazan gorge of the Danube
veg: Steppe with patches of pine and spruce woodland. Sources: 'Looking around Peştera cu Oase' (Quaternary International, 2012); Davis et al. 2024, Climate of the Past 20, 1939.

name: Moravia, on the mammoth steppe
veg: Mammoth steppe with islands of taiga (larch, spruce, pine). Sources: Jankovská & Pokorný 2008; REVEALS late Last Glacial (ESSD 17, 5997, 2025).

name: the Vézère valley, in the Dordogne
veg: Cold steppe with pine and birch in sheltered valleys. Source: Davis et al. 2024, Climate of the Past 20, 1939 (LGM pollen).

name: Doggerland, between Britain and Europe
veg: Grassy tundra and dwarf-shrub heath with a few trees along the rivers. Sources: Life in Doggerland (E&G Quat. Sci. J. 66, 2017); Allaby et al. 2026 (PNAS, sedaDNA).

name: the middle Danube valley
labels: early farmers' village, a little later
veg: Mixed oak, elm and lime forest with open floodplain meadows, before farming. Sources: LBK woodland studies (Saqalli et al. 2014, Veg. Hist. Archaeobot.).

name: the Argolid, in Greece
veg: Deciduous oak woodland and maquis on the hills; cereal fields on the plain. Source: the Lake Lerna pollen record (PLoS ONE, 2022).

name: the Tiber valley, in Latium
veg: Deciduous oak forest with clearings, meadows and floodplain wetland. Sources: Lago Albano and Nemi pollen (Mercuri et al. 2002); Bernard et al. 2023 (J. Interdiscip. Hist.).
